raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Branch: mick/diffusion-scale-shift-row-tiles (on main efd2ce8a9d), commit ca74a81722

## Motivation

`fuse_scale_shift_kernel`'s `[B, L, C]` path (`MulAdd` - Wan's FFN gated residual - and the native norm modulation) launches 128x128 tiles, which read each row in 256-byte pieces. On Wan2.2 A14B 720p (`[1, 37800, 5120]` per rank) the kernel moved 1.16 GB in 0.29 ms in isolation and 0.35 ms inside the denoising loop: one of the slowest elementwise kernels in the block.

B300, bf16 x, fp32 gate `[1, 1, C]`, bf16 shift `[B, L, C]`:

| B, L, C | 128x128 | rows x 1024 | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 37800, 5120 | 0.2933 ms | 0.1851 ms | 1.58x |
| 2, 4096, 3072 | 0.0449 ms | 0.0273 ms | 1.65x |
| 1, 4608, 3072 | 0.0189 ms | 0.0183 ms | 1.04x |
| 1, 75600, 1536 | 0.1766 ms | 0.1144 ms | 1.54x |
| 2, 8192, 2560 | 0.0681 ms | 0.0435 ms | 1.56x |
| 1, 32760, 4096 | 0.2041 ms | 0.1315 ms | 1.55x |
| 1, 1000, 5120 | 0.0193 ms | 0.0180 ms | 1.07x |
| 1, 37800, 3840 | 0.2209 ms | 0.1392 ms | 1.59x |

## Modifications

`kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/scale_shift_triton.py`: on NVIDIA GPUs the 3D path launches up to 1024 channels by `4096 / BLOCK_C` rows per program. The per-element arithmetic is unchanged, so the output is bit-identical. ROCm and XPU keep their tiles.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_modulate.py::test_scale_shift_3d_tiling_is_bit_exact`: the new tiling equals a 128x128 launch of the same kernel bitwise (C from 96 to 5120, scale constant 0 and 1), and stays within the existing tolerance of the eager formula.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Wan2.2 T2V A14B 720p, 4xB300, CFG 2 x Ulysses 2: MulAdd 0.349 -> ~0.2 ms per block. E2E, two interleaved rounds of fresh servers, 3 requests each: 91.230 / 91.381 / 91.436 / 91.332 / 91.321 / 91.347 s (median 91.34) -> 91.283 / 91.254 / 91.268 / 91.226 / 91.220 / 91.317 s (median 91.26). The GPUs run at their power cap through the denoise, so a bandwidth-bound kernel's saving shows up at about half its length.

@@ -11,6 +11,7 @@
 
 import pytest
 import torch
+import triton
 
 from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import get_ci_test_range
 from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
@@ -30,6 +31,9 @@
     timestep_embedding,
     try_fused_scaled_residual_add_exact,
 )
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.modulate.scale_shift_triton import (
+    fuse_scale_shift_kernel_blc_opt,
+)
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci, register_cuda_ci
 
 register_cuda_ci(est_time=75, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
@@ -135,6 +139,52 @@ def test_scale_shift_4d_matches_torch(shape, num_frames, dtype, scale_constant):
     torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=5e-2, rtol=5e-2)
 
 
+# Wan's MulAdd (fp32 gate) and its LayerNorm modulation (fp32 scale/shift).
+SCALE_SHIFT_3D_CASES = [(1, 37, 5120), (2, 9, 1536), (1, 5, 3072), (1, 3, 96)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", SCALE_SHIFT_3D_CASES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scale_constant", [0, 1])
+def test_scale_shift_3d_tiling_is_bit_exact(shape, scale_constant):
+    """The row tiling gives the bytes of the 128x128 tile it replaced."""
+    batch, seq_len, hidden = shape
+    x = torch.randn(shape, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    scale = torch.randn((1, 1, hidden), device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.float32)
+    shift = torch.randn_like(x)
+    actual = fuse_scale_shift_kernel(x, scale, shift, scale_constant)
+
+    expected = torch.empty_like(x)
+    scale_exp = scale.expand(batch, seq_len, hidden)
+    fuse_scale_shift_kernel_blc_opt[
+        (triton.cdiv(seq_len, 128), triton.cdiv(hidden, 128), batch)
+    ](
+        x,
+        shift,
+        scale_exp,
+        scale_constant,
+        expected,
+        batch,
+        seq_len,
+        hidden,
+        *x.stride(),
+        *shift.stride(),
+        *scale_exp.stride(),
+        SCALE_IS_SCALAR=False,
+        SHIFT_IS_SCALAR=False,
+        BLOCK_L=128,
+        BLOCK_C=128,
+        num_warps=4,
+        num_stages=2,
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(actual, expected)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        actual.float(),
+        x.float() * (scale_constant + scale) + shift.float(),
+        atol=5e-2,
+        rtol=5e-2,
+    )
+
+
